name: an-authenticated-plugin-is-welcomed-and-served
description: A protocol client upgrades, says hello with the token and is welcomed with the app version and the snapshot, each message in its own frame. Its intents reach the app, a ping message gets a pong message and a ping frame a pong frame with the same payload; a second hello does nothing; the idle deadline spares it. Its close frame is answered with 1000 and nothing after it is read. A hello split across reads waits for its frame.
reason: This is the local plugin API's happy path (docs/protocol.md); every later rule is a departure from it (HK-234, HK-256 to HK-258).
verifiedBy: DESIGN.md v1.4, v1.7; docs/protocol.md spec v0. Rust: rust/powerup-core/tests/listener.rs listener_scenarios plays every step through protocol::listener::Listener. Swift: Tests/PowerUpTests/ListenerScenarioTests.swift testEveryListenerScenario plays every step through the bridge (CoreBridge.ListenerPolicy), and ProtocolServerTests drives the same policy over a real loopback socket.

steps.reason: Settings start the listener: the start stops first (generation 1), then binds 127.0.0.1 with generation 2 (RemoteListener.swift:79-135).
The bind is ready: running, no problem (RemoteListener.swift:158-161).
A socket is accepted: it becomes connection 1 under the 15-second deadline (RemoteListener.swift:222-257, 427-433).

steps.reason: The app answers the welcome effect: welcome, then status and session (RemoteListener.swift:269-275).
An intent from an authenticated client reaches the app, its prompt trimmed (RemoteListener.swift:691-698).
Another intent.
A ping message gets a pong message.
A ping frame gets a pong frame echoing its payload (RemoteListener.swift:656-657).
An unsolicited pong frame is ignored.
A second hello does nothing, even with a wrong token (RemoteListener.swift:680).
The deadline spares an authenticated client (RemoteListener.swift:427-433).

A close frame is answered with close 1000 and the connection closed; the intent behind it in the same read is not handled (the core reads nothing after a close; Swift handled it until its close completed).
A closing connection reads nothing.
The close has run.
A socket is accepted: it becomes connection 2 under the 15-second deadline (RemoteListener.swift:222-257, 427-433).
